facts.statement: Ornitholestes is known from a single partial skeleton with a crushed skull found at Bone Cabin Quarry in Wyoming in 1900.
facts.quote: To date, Ornitholestes is known only from a single partial skeleton with a badly crushed skull found at the Bone Cabin Quarry near Medicine Bow, Wyoming, in 1900.

facts.statement: Henry Fairfield Osborn described Ornitholestes in 1903.
facts.quote: It was described by Henry Fairfield Osborn in 1903.

facts.statement: Ornitholestes was the first theropod dinosaur discovered in the 1900s.
facts.quote: Ornitholestes was the first theropod to be discovered in the 1900s.

facts.statement: The genus name Ornitholestes, suggested by Theodore Gill, means "bird robber" in Ancient Greek.
facts.quote: The genus name Ornitholestes, initially suggested by Theodore Gill, comes from Ancient Greek ὄρνις (órnis), meaning "bird", and λῃστής (lēistḗs), meaning "robber".

facts.statement: The species name O. hermanni honors Adam Hermann, the museum preparator who restored and mounted the skeleton.
facts.quote: The species name (O. hermanni) honors Adam Hermann, the head preparator at the Museum, who directed the restoration and mounting of the skeleton.

facts.statement: Henry Fairfield Osborn assigned an incomplete hand (AMNH 587) to Ornitholestes in his 1903 description.
facts.quote: An incomplete hand (AMNH 587) was assigned to Ornitholestes by Osborn in his 1903 description of the genus.

facts.statement: In 2005, Kenneth Carpenter et al. described Tanycolagreus, a new theropod found near the hand previously attributed to Ornitholestes.
facts.quote: In 2005, Kenneth Carpenter et al. described a new small theropod, Tanycolagreus, whose skeleton was found in Bone Cabin Quarry only a few hundred yards from AMNH 587.

facts.statement: The hand AMNH 587 is now considered to belong to Tanycolagreus rather than Ornitholestes.
facts.quote: Since AMNH 587 was virtually identical to the preserved hand of the Tanycolagreus type specimen, it is now considered to belong to that dinosaur and not to Ornitholestes.

facts.statement: After reassigning the hand to Tanycolagreus, knowledge of Ornitholestes relies solely on the holotype specimen.
facts.quote: Following this reassignment, Phil Senter (2006) noted that "our knowledge of Ornitholestes can be drawn now only from the holotype."

facts.statement: John Foster reported in 2007 that fragments from Dry Mesa Quarry might belong to Ornitholestes, but they remain undescribed.
facts.quote: John Foster (2007) reported that some fragments from Dry Mesa Quarry may belong to Ornitholestes, though these have not yet been described.

facts.statement: Ornitholestes was once considered identical to Coelurus, then treated as a species of Coelurus, before being revived as a distinct genus in 1980.
facts.quote: In 1920 Charles Whitney Gilmore concluded that Ornitholestes was identical to Coelurus; in 1934 Oliver Perry Hay recognised only a difference at the species level, naming a Coelurus hermanni, but in 1980 John Ostrom revived the genus.

facts.statement: Ornitholestes lived about 154 million years ago in the late Jurassic of what is now North America.
facts.quote: Ornitholestes (from Ancient Greek ὄρνις (órnis), meaning "bird", and λῃστής (lēistḗs), meaning "robber", and thus, "bird robber") is a small theropod dinosaur of the late Jurassic (Brushy Basin Member of the Morrison Formation, middle Kimmeridgian age, about 154 million years ago) of Western Laurasia (the area that was to become North America).

facts.statement: Henry Fairfield Osborn originally estimated the length of Ornitholestes at 2.22 meters.
facts.quote: In his 1903 description, Osborn wrote that the length of Ornitholestes along "the skull and vertebral column as restored" was 2.22 m.

facts.statement: David Norman and John Foster estimated that Ornitholestes was about 2 meters long.
facts.quote: David Norman (1985) and John Foster (2007) both estimated that Ornitholestes was about 2 m long.

facts.statement: Gregory S. Paul estimated the length of Ornitholestes at approximately 2.08 meters in 1988.
facts.quote: Gregory S. Paul's 1988 Predatory Dinosaurs of the World listed the length of Ornitholestes as approximately 2.08 m.

facts.statement: Gregory S. Paul and John Foster both estimated the weight of Ornitholestes at 12.6 kilograms.
facts.quote: Paul (1988) and Foster (2007) both estimated that Ornitholestes weighed 12.6 kg.

facts.statement: John A. Long and Peter Schouten suggested the weight of Ornitholestes was 15 kilograms.
facts.quote: John A. Long and Peter Schouten (2008) suggested a slightly higher figure, 15 kg.

facts.statement: Ornitholestes was a bipedal carnivore.
facts.quote: Ornitholestes was a bipedal carnivore.

facts.statement: Ornitholestes had a proportionally small head with a heavily built skull, short snout, and robust lower jaw.
facts.quote: Its head was proportionally smaller than that of most other predatory dinosaurs, but the skull was heavily built, with a short snout and robust lower jaw.

facts.statement: The eye sockets of Ornitholestes measured over 25 percent of the skull's length.
facts.quote: The orbits (eye sockets) were quite large, measuring over 25 percent of the skull's length.

facts.statement: Ornitholestes had conical front teeth with reduced serrations and recurved, sharply serrated back teeth.
facts.quote: The front teeth of Ornitholestes were somewhat conical, with reduced serrations; the back teeth were recurved and more sharply serrated, similar to those of other theropod dinosaurs.

facts.statement: Henry Fairfield Osborn counted four teeth in the premaxilla, with the front tooth being the largest in the upper jaw.
facts.quote: Henry Fairfield Osborn (1903) counted four teeth in the premaxilla, of which the front tooth was the largest in the upper jaw.

facts.statement: Ornitholestes had ten teeth in each maxilla and twelve teeth in each dentary.
facts.quote: Each maxilla (main tooth-bearing bone in the upper jaw) contained ten teeth, and each dentary (tooth-bearing bone in the lower jaw) contained twelve teeth.

facts.statement: The tail of Ornitholestes was long and whiplike, making up over half of its body length.
facts.quote: The tail was long and whiplike, comprising over half of the body's length.

facts.statement: Carpenter et al. recorded that the Ornitholestes specimen contained five sacral vertebrae.
facts.quote: Carpenter et al. (2005a) recorded that the specimen contained five sacral vertebrae.

facts.statement: The humerus of Ornitholestes was heavily built and longer than the radius and ulna.
facts.quote: The humerus (upper arm bone) was heavily built, and somewhat longer than the radius and ulna (forearm bones).

facts.statement: Osborn calculated that the missing tibia of Ornitholestes was about 70.6% the length of the femur.
facts.quote: Osborn (1917) calculated that the, missing, tibia (shin bone) was only about 70.6% as long as the femur (thigh bone).

facts.statement: John H. Ostrom suggested that the innermost toe of Ornitholestes may have had a modified sickle claw similar to Deinonychus.
facts.quote: John H. Ostrom (1969) noted that the claw of digit II (the innermost toe) was larger than those of digits III and IV, and suggested that this digit may have borne a modified sickle claw similar to that of Deinonychus.

facts.statement: The hypothesis that Ornitholestes had a modified sickle claw is difficult to confirm due to poor preservation of the toe.
facts.quote: However, as both Ostrom (1969) and Paul (1988) noted, the poor preservation of digit II makes this hypothesis difficult to confirm.

facts.statement: Gregory S. Paul suggested in 1988 that a bulge near the nostril indicated a nasal horn resembling a chicken's comb.
facts.quote: An area of broken bone near the external naris (nostril) appears to bulge upward, which led Gregory S. Paul to suggest in Predatory Dinosaurs of the World (1988) that Ornitholestes had a nasal horn "rather like a chicken's comb in looks."

facts.statement: Oliver W.M. Rauhut and Kenneth Carpenter et al. rejected the idea of a nasal horn, attributing the bone bulge to post-mortem crushing.
facts.quote: Both Oliver W.M. Rauhut (2003) and Kenneth Carpenter et al. (2005a) rejected that interpretation, and indicated that the upward flare of bone was due to post-mortem crushing of the skull.

facts.statement: All known information about Ornitholestes comes from a single specimen discovered in 1900 at the Bone Cabin Mine near Medicine Bow, Wyoming, and described by Henry Fairfield Osborn in 1903.
facts.quote: Todo lo que se sabe sobre Ornitholestes se debe de un solo espécimen descubierto en 1900 en la Mina Bone Cabin cerca de Medicine Bow, Wyoming, y descrito por Henry Fairfield Osborn en 1903.

facts.statement: Ornitholestes lived during the Late Jurassic, approximately 157 million years ago, from the Kimmeridgian to the Tithonian stages, in what is now North America.
facts.quote: que vivió a finales del período Jurásico, hace aproximadamente entre 157 million years ago, desde el Kimmeridgiense al Titoniense, en lo que hoy es Norteamérica.

facts.statement: Ornitholestes was an agile carnivore that lived in forested habitats.
facts.quote: Era un carnívoro ágil que vivió en hábitats boscosos.

facts.statement: Ornitholestes likely fed on lizards and mammals, though it may also have been an opportunistic scavenger.
facts.quote: Probablemente se haya alimentado de lagartos y mamíferos; aunque también pudo haber sido un carroñero oportunista.

facts.statement: All published cladistic analyses classify Ornitholestes as a coelurosaur as defined by Gauthier.
facts.quote: All published cladistic analyses have shown Ornitholestes to be a coelurosaur as defined by Gauthier.

facts.statement: Kimberley Chapelle and colleagues presented robust evidence in 2021 suggesting Ornitholestes is the earliest-diverging oviraptorosaur based on CT scan analysis of the skull.
facts.quote: In an abstract presented at the 2021 conference of the Society of Vertebrate Paleontology, Kimberley Chapelle and colleagues found "robust evidence" that Ornitholestes is the earliest-diverging oviraptorosaur, based on a CT scan analysis of the skull.

facts.statement: A 2001 study by Bruce Rothschild and colleagues examined 20 foot bones of Ornitholestes and found no signs of stress fractures.
facts.quote: In a 2001 study conducted by Bruce Rothschild and other paleontologists, 20 foot bones referred to Ornitholestes were examined for signs of stress fracture, but none were found.

facts.statement: When the elbow of Ornitholestes was flexed to its maximum extent, the humerus and radius formed a 53° angle.
facts.quote: When flexed (bent inward) at the elbow joint to the maximum possible extent, the humerus (upper arm bone) and radius (a lower arm bone) formed a 53° angle.

facts.statement: Ornitholestes may have used its ability to bend its elbows inward to grasp prey with both hands simultaneously.
facts.quote: It may have used that ability to grasp prey with both hands simultaneously.

facts.statement: In 1903, Henry Fairfield Osborn interpreted the large conical front teeth, rapid grasping hand, and balancing tail of Ornitholestes as adaptations for preying on contemporary birds.
facts.quote: Henry Fairfield Osborn, in his 1903 description of Ornitholestes, noted its large and conical front teeth, the "rapid grasping power" of its hand, and the "balancing power" of its tail; these he interpreted as adaptations to prey on contemporary birds.

facts.statement: Most recent authors suggest that Ornitholestes had a diet of small terrestrial vertebrates.
facts.quote: Most recent authors, however, have instead suggested a diet of small terrestrial vertebrates.

facts.statement: Gregory S. Paul estimated in 1988 that a 12 kg endothermic Ornitholestes would require about 700 g of flesh daily.
facts.quote: Paul (1988) estimated that a 12 kg endothermic Ornitholestes would have a daily dietary requirement of about 700 g of flesh.

facts.statement: The 1996 discovery of Sinosauropteryx in China revealed a coat of rudimentary furlike feathers.
facts.quote: In 1996, the primitive coelurosaur Sinosauropteryx was discovered in China. The well-preserved fossil showed that this dinosaur bore a coat of rudimentary furlike feathers.

facts.statement: John Foster inferred in 2007 that Ornitholestes likely had primitive feathers covering the body except the legs, possibly with longer feathers on the skull, neck, and forearm edges.
facts.quote: Based on its phylogenetic position, John Foster (2007) inferred that the feathers of Ornitholestes would probably have been more primitive than those of birds; they likely "would have covered the body except the legs in a short coat, perhaps with longer feathers lining the top of the skull or neck and the back edge of the forearms."

facts.statement: Ornitholestes is a coelurosaurian similar in many aspects to Compsognathus, though much longer.
facts.quote: Ornitholestes es un celurosauriano, similar en muchos aspectos a Compsognathus, aunque mucho más largo.

facts.statement: Charles R. Knight's influential illustration of Ornitholestes chasing Archaeopteryx appeared in popular dinosaur books throughout the 20th century.
facts.quote: Knight's illustration, and others derived from it, continued to appear in dinosaur books aimed at a popular audience throughout the 20th century.

facts.statement: Ornitholestes is classified within the subfamily Ornitholestinae.
facts.quote: subfamilia: Ornitholestinae

facts.statement: The genus Ornitholestes was named by Osborn in 1903.
facts.quote: genus_authority: Osborn, 1903

facts.statement: The species O. hermanni was named by Osborn in 1903.
facts.quote: species_authority: Osborn, 1903

facts.statement: Its head was proportionally smaller than most other dinosaur predators, but the skull was strongly built with a short snout and a robust lower jaw.
facts.quote: Su cabeza era proporcionalmente más pequeña que la de la mayoría de los otros dinosaurios depredadores, pero el cráneo estaba fuertemente construido, con un hocico corto y una mandíbula inferior robusta.

facts.statement: Its eye sockets were quite large, measuring more than 25 percent of the skull length.
facts.quote: Las órbitas, cuencas de los ojos, eran bastante grandes, midiendo más del 25 por ciento de la longitud del cráneo.

facts.statement: There is no evidence of an orbital bone ring.
facts.quote: No hay indicios de un anillo ocular óseo.

facts.statement: Ornitholestes was a ceratosaurian similar in many ways to Compsognathus but larger, reaching just over 2 meters in length, 0.80 meters in height, and an estimated weight of 13 kilograms.
facts.quote: Ornitholestes era un celurosauriano, similar en muchas formas al Compsognathus, pero de mayor tamaño, llegando a medir poco más de 2 metros de largo y 0.80 de alto, con un peso estimado de 13 kilogramos.

facts.statement: It possessed small, serrated teeth and possibly hunted small animals such as lizards and mammals.
facts.quote: Poseía pequeños y aserrados dientes y posiblemente cazara pequeños animales como lagartijas y mamíferos.

facts.statement: The skull is more robust compared to other small theropods like Compsognathus and Coelophysis, which likely gave Ornitholestes a powerful bite.
facts.quote: El cráneo es más robusto, comparado con otros pequeños terópodos, como Compsognathus y Coelophysis, lo que le debe haber dado a Ornitholestes una poderosa mordida.

facts.statement: The front teeth of Ornitholestes were somewhat conical with reduced serrations.
facts.quote: Los dientes frontales de Ornitholestes eran algo cónicos, con estrías reducidas.

facts.statement: The rear teeth were recurved and more serrated, similar to those of other theropod dinosaurs.
facts.quote: Los dientes posteriores eran recurvados y más aserrados, similares a los de otros dinosaurios terópodos.

facts.statement: In 1903, Henry Fairfield Osborn counted four teeth in the premaxilla, with the front tooth being the largest in the upper jaw.
facts.quote: Henry Fairfield Osborn en 1903 contó cuatro dientes en el premaxilar, de los cuales el diente frontal era el más grande en la mandíbula superior.

facts.statement: In contrast, Gregory S. Paul described the skull in 1988 as having only three remaining premaxillary teeth, much smaller than those illustrated by Osborn.
facts.quote: En contraste, Gregory S. Paul en 1988 describió el cráneo con solo tres dientes premaxilares restantes, mucho más pequeños que los ilustrados por Osborn.

facts.statement: Each maxilla, the main bone holding teeth in the upper jaw, contained ten teeth, and each dentary in the lower jaw contained twelve teeth.
facts.quote: Cada maxilar, principal hueso que sostiene a los dientes en la mandíbula superior, contenía diez, y cada dentario, en la mandíbula inferior, contenía doce dientes.

facts.statement: The rows of teeth were short, with the lower dentary row even shorter than the upper maxillary row, despite the dentary bone being exceptionally long in the rear, reaching a point below the center of the eye socket.
facts.quote: Las filas de dientes de Ornitholestes eran cortas, con la fila dentaria inferior aún más corta que la fila maxilar superior, a pesar de que el hueso dentaria era excepcionalmente largo en la parte posterior, llegando a un punto por debajo del centro de la cavidad del ojo.

facts.statement: The teeth did not extend as far as the orbits, and no row of teeth spanned more than one-third of the skull.
facts.quote: Los dientes no se extendían tanto como las órbitas, y ninguna fila de dientes abarcaba mucho más de un tercio del cráneo.

facts.statement: The serrated teeth clearly identify Ornitholestes as a carnivore, but its exact diet is a matter of debate in the paleontological community.
facts.quote: Los dientes aserrados de Ornitholestes lo identifican claramente como un carnívoro, pero su dieta exacta es motivo de debate en la comunidad paleontológica.

facts.statement: In the original 1903 description, Henry Fairfield Osborn suggested that Ornitholestes must have eaten contemporary birds, based on the "rapid and powerful grasping of agile and delicate prey" suggested by the hand shape.
facts.quote: En la descripción original de 1903, Henry Fairfield Osborn sugiere que Ornitholestes debió haber comido aves contemporáneas, basado en la "aprensión rápida y poderosa de ágiles y delicadas presas" sugerida por la forma de la mano.

facts.statement: However, in 1917, Osborn re-evaluated the hand and determined it was inadequate for this purpose.
facts.quote: En 1917, sin embargo, Osborn evaluó de nuevo la mano y determinó que era inadecuada para este fin.

facts.statement: More recently, Robert T. Bakker has speculated that Ornitholestes probably hunted small mammals, noting that "pellet balls were about the exact size of the predator's jaws."
facts.quote: Más recientemente, Robert T. Bakker ha especulado que Ornitholestes probablemente cazara pequeños mamíferos, notando que "las bolas de pelos de como eran del tamaño exacto de la mandíbulas del predador."

facts.statement: A broken bone area near the external nostril seemed to bulge upward, leading Gregory S. Paul to suggest the presence of a small horn on the snout of Ornitholestes, similar to Proceratosaurus, "like a chicken's crest in appearance."
facts.quote: Un área de hueso roto cerca de la nariz externa, orificio nasal, parece abultarse hacia arriba, lo que llevó a Gregory S. Paul sugerir la presencia de un pequeño cuerno en el hocico del Ornitholestes, similar al de Proceratosaurus, "como la cresta de un pollo en apariencia".

facts.statement: Both Oliver WM Rauhut in 2003 and Kenneth Carpenter et al. in 2005 rejected this interpretation and indicated that the upward flare of the bone was due to post-mortem crushing of the skull.
facts.quote: Tanto Oliver WM Rauhut en 2003 como Kenneth Carpenter et al. en 2005 rechazaron esa interpretación e indicaron que el destello ascendente del hueso se debió al aplastamiento post mortem del cráneo.

facts.statement: Ornitholestes had a relatively short neck with a slight S-shaped sigmoid curve.
facts.quote: Ornitholestes tenía un cuello relativamente corto con una ligera curva sigmoidea, en forma de S.

facts.statement: The tail was long and whip-like, spanning more than half the body length, presumably to aid in balance.
facts.quote: La cola era larga y en forma de látigo, y abarcaba más de la mitad de la longitud del cuerpo, presumiblemente para favorecer el balance.

facts.statement: Osborn estimated in 1917 that Ornitholestes had nine or ten cervical vertebrae, thirteen dorsal vertebrae, four sacral vertebrae, and 39 to 44 caudal vertebrae.
facts.quote: Osborn en 1917 estimó que Ornitholestes tenía nueve o diez vértebras cervicales, trece vértebras dorsales, cuatro vértebras sacras y 39 a 44 caudales.

facts.statement: Carpenter and colleagues recorded in 2005 that the specimen contained five sacral vertebrae.
facts.quote: Carpenter y colaboradores en 2005 registraron que el espécimen contenía cinco vértebras sacras.

facts.statement: Ornitholestes was a short-bodied theropod, reflected in the short front-to-back dimensions of the cervical and dorsal vertebrae.
facts.quote: Ornitholestes era un terópodo de cuerpo corto, y esto se reflejó en las dimensiones cortas de adelante hacia atrás de las vértebras cervicales y dorsales.

facts.statement: The forelimbs of Ornitholestes were relatively long, slightly less than two-thirds the length of the hind legs.
facts.quote: Las extremidades anteriores de Ornitholestes eran relativamente largas, un poco menos de dos tercios del largo de las patas traseras.

facts.statement: The humerus, the bone of the upper arm, was strongly built and slightly longer than the radius and ulna, the forearm bones.
facts.quote: El húmero, hueso de la parte superior del brazo, estaba fuertemente construido y algo más largo que el radio y el cúbito, huesos del antebrazo.

facts.statement: Both the humerus and radius were straight in axis.
facts.quote: Tanto el húmero como el radio eran de eje recto.

facts.statement: The claws on digits I and II of the hand were approximately the same size.
facts.quote: Las garras en los dígitos I y II de la mano eran aproximadamente del mismo tamaño.

facts.statement: Although the third ungual of the hand, the claw bone, was not preserved, extrapolation from Ornitholestes' closest relatives indicates it was probably shorter than the first two.
facts.quote: Aunque el tercer ungual de la mano, hueso de la garra, no se conservó, la extrapolación de los parientes más cercanos de Ornitholestes indica que probablemente fue más corto que los dos primeros.

facts.statement: Ornitholestes was the first theropod discovered in the 1900s.
facts.quote: Ornitholestes fue el primer terópodo descubierto en la década de 1900.

facts.statement: The holotype skeleton AMNH 619 was excavated in July 1900 at the Bone Cabin Quarry in Wyoming by an expedition from the American Museum of Natural History led by Peter C. Kaisen, Paul Miller, and Frederic Brewster Loomis.
facts.quote: El esqueleto holotipo AMNH 619 fue excavado en julio de 1900 en la Cantera Bone Cabin en Wyoming por una expedición del Museo Americano de Historia Natural por Peter C. Kaisen, Paul Miller y Frederic Brewster Loomis.

facts.statement: It represents a partial skeleton with a skull, including numerous elements of the vertebral column, forelimbs, pelvis, and hind limbs.
facts.quote: Representa un esqueleto parcial con cráneo, que incluye numerosos elementos de la columna vertebral, las extremidades anteriores, la pelvis y las extremidades posteriores.

facts.statement: Henry Fairfield Osborn named and scientifically described the specimen in 1903.
facts.quote: Henry Fairfield Osborn nombró y describió científicamente el espécimen en 1903.

facts.statement: The genus name Ornitholestes, initially suggested by Theodore Gill, means "bird thief" and is derived from the Greek ὄρνις, ornis, ornithos, "bird" and λῃστήσ, lestes, "thief."
facts.quote: El nombre del género Ornitholestes, inicialmente sugerido por Theodore Gill, significa "ladrón de pájaros" y se deriva del griego ὄρνις, ornis, ornithos, "pájaro" y λῃστήσ, lestes, "ladrón".

facts.statement: The species name, O. hermanni, honors Adam Hermann, the museum's chief preparator, who directed the restoration and assembly of the skeleton.
facts.quote: El nombre de la especie, O. hermanni, honra a Adam Hermann, el preparador principal del Museo, quien dirigió la restauración y el montaje del esqueleto.

facts.statement: Osborn assigned an incomplete hand, AMNH 587, to Ornitholestes in his 1903 description of the genus.
facts.quote: Osborn asignó una mano incompleta, AMNH 587, a Ornitholestes en su descripción de 1903 del género.

facts.statement: However, as Gregory S. Paul noted in 1988, the poor preservation of the corresponding elements in the type specimen made this association "provisional."
facts.quote: Sin embargo, como señaló Gregory S. Paul en 1988, la preservación deficiente de los elementos correspondientes en el espécimen tipo hizo que esta asociación sea "provisional".

facts.statement: In 2005, Kenneth Carpenter et al. described a new small theropod, Tanycolagreus, whose skeleton was found at the Bone Cabin Quarry only a few hundred yards from AMNH 587.
facts.quote: En 2005, Kenneth Carpenter et al. describió un nuevo terópodo pequeño, Tanycolagreus, cuyo esqueleto se encontró en la Cantera de la Cabaña de Huesos a solo unos cientos de yardas de AMNH 587.

facts.statement: Since AMNH 587 was virtually identical to the preserved hand of the Tanycolagreus type specimen, it is now considered to belong to that dinosaur and not Ornitholestes.
facts.quote: Como AMNH 587 era prácticamente idéntico a la mano preservada del espécimen tipo Tanycolagreus, ahora se considera que pertenece a ese dinosaurio y no a Ornitholestes.

facts.statement: After this reassignment, Phil Senter noted in 2006 that "our knowledge of Ornitholestes can now be drawn only from the holotype."
facts.quote: Luego de esta reasignación, Phil Senter en 2006 señaló que "nuestro conocimiento de Ornitholestes ahora puede extraerse solo del holotipo".

facts.statement: John Foster reported in 2007 that some fragments from the Dry Mesa Quarry may belong to Ornitholestes, although they have not yet been described.
facts.quote: John Foster en 2007 informó que algunos fragmentos de la Cabntera Dry Mesa pueden pertenecer a Ornitholestes, aunque todavía no se han descrito.

facts.statement: In 1920, Charles Whitney Gilmore concluded that Ornitholestes was identical to Coelurus.
facts.quote: En 1920 Charles Whitney Gilmore concluyó que Ornitholestes era idéntico a Coelurus.

facts.statement: In 1934, Oliver Perry Hay recognized only a species-level difference, naming Coelurus hermanni, but in 1980 John Ostrom revived the genus.
facts.quote: en 1934 Oliver Perry Hay reconoció solo una diferencia a nivel de especie, nombrando un Coelurus hermanni, pero en 1980 John Ostrom revivió el género.

facts.statement: In a 2001 study by Bruce Rothschild and other paleontologists, 20 foot bones referred to Ornitholestes were examined for signs of stress fractures, but none were found.
facts.quote: En un estudio realizado en 2001 por Bruce Rothschild y otros paleontólogos, se examinaron 20 huesos del pie referidos a Ornitholestes para detectar signos de fractura por estrés, pero no se encontraron ninguno.

facts.statement: When fully flexed, Ornitholestes could bend its elbow to a maximum angle of 53 degrees between the upper arm bone and forearm bones.
facts.quote: Cuando se flexionó, dobló hacia adentro, en la articulación del codo al máximo posible, el húmero, hueso del brazo superior y el radio, un hueso del brazo inferior formaron un ángulo de 53°.

facts.statement: The ability to bend the forearm at an angle significantly sharper than 90 degrees is characteristic of Maniraptoriformes but absent in more primitive theropods like Coelophysis and Allosaurus.
facts.quote: La capacidad de Ornitholestes para doblar el antebrazo en un ángulo significativamente más agudo que 90° es característica de Maniraptoriformes, pero ausente en terópodos más primitivos como Coelophysis y Allosaurus.

facts.statement: Even when fully extended, Ornitholestes' elbow did not form a right angle, leaving the forearm short by 22 degrees.
facts.quote: Incluso cuando estaba completamente extendido el codo, el antebrazo no formó un ángulo recto, quedando corto en 22°.

facts.statement: Pronation was impossible for Ornitholestes because its radius and ulna lacked rolling surfaces, meaning its forearm was permanently in a supinated state.
facts.quote: La pronación, girando para hacer que el lado palmar de la mano mire hacia abajo del antebrazo era imposible, porque el radio y el cúbito carecían de superficies rodantes, lo que significa que el antebrazo estaba en un estado permanente de supinación.

facts.statement: Researchers suggest Ornitholestes may have used its ability to bend elbows inward to grab prey with both hands simultaneously.
facts.quote: Puede haber usado esa habilidad para agarrar presas con ambas manos simultáneamente.

facts.statement: In his 1903 description, Henry Fairfield Osborn interpreted Ornitholestes' large conical front teeth, rapid hand grip, and balancing tail as adaptations for preying on contemporary birds.
facts.quote: Henry Fairfield Osborn, en su descripción de Ornitholestes de 1903, notó sus dientes frontales grandes y cónicos, el "poder de agarre rápido" de su mano y el "poder de equilibrio" de su cola y los interpretó como adaptaciones para aprovecharse de las aves contemporáneas.

facts.statement: David Norman in 1985 admitted it was simply possible, though unlikely, that Ornitholestes could have trapped and eaten primitive birds.
facts.quote: David Norman en 1985 admitió que era "simplemente posible, aunque no muy probable" que Ornitholestes pudiera haber atrapado y comido aves primitivas.

facts.statement: Recent authors suggest Ornitholestes had a diet of small terrestrial vertebrates.
facts.quote: los autores más recientes han sugerido una dieta de pequeños vertebrados terrestres.

facts.statement: Possible prey for Ornitholestes included mammals, lizards, frogs, salamanders, temnospondyls, and dinosaur hatchlings.
facts.quote: Mamíferos, lagartos, ranas, salamandras, rincocéfalos y crías de dinosaurios habrían sido posibles presas.

facts.statement: Gregory S. Paul in 1988 thought Ornitholestes might have used its conical front teeth to fish.
facts.quote: Gregory S. Paul en 1988 pensó que Ornitholestes podría haber utilizado sus dientes frontales cónicos para pescar.

facts.statement: David Norman in 1985 suggested Ornitholestes' robust skull and jaws might have allowed it to handle larger and more active prey than other small theropods.
facts.quote: Norman en 1985 sugirió que el cráneo y las mandíbulas robustos podrían haber permitido a Ornitholestes hacer frente a "presas más grandes y más activas" que otros pequeños terópodos.

facts.statement: In 2007, John Foster suggested a possible niche division between similarly sized Ornitholestes and its contemporary Coelurus.
facts.quote: En 2007, John Foster, especialista en la Formación Morrison, sugirió la posibilidad de una división de nicho entre Ornitholestes y su contemporáneo Coelurus, que estaba dentro del mismo rango de tamaño.

facts.statement: Foster theorized that Ornitholestes, with its large eyes, might have specialized in nocturnal hunting while Coelurus focused on diurnal prey.
facts.quote: Teorizó que Ornitholestes de ojos grandes podría haberse especializado en la caza nocturna, mientras que Coelurus podría haberse centrado en las especies de presas que estaban activas durante el día.

facts.statement: Paul in 1988 estimated an endothermic 12-kilogram Ornitholestes would have a daily dietary requirement of approximately 700 grams of meat.
facts.quote: Paul 1988 estimó que un Ornitholestes endotérmico de 12 kilogramos tendría un requerimiento dietético diario de aproximadamente 700 gramos de carne.

facts.statement: Ornithologist Percy Lowe proposed in 1944 that Ornitholestes might have had feathers.
facts.quote: El ornitólogo Percy Lowe planteó la hipótesis en 1944 de que Ornitholestes podría tener plumas.

facts.statement: Based on its phylogenetic position, John Foster inferred in 2007 that Ornitholestes' feathers were likely more primitive than birds', probably covering the body except the legs with a short coat, perhaps with longer feathers on the top of the skull, neck, and rear edge of the forearms.
facts.quote: Basado en su posición filogenética, John Foster en 2007 infirió que las plumas de Ornitholestes probablemente habrían sido más primitivas que las de las aves, probablemente "habrían cubierto el cuerpo, excepto las piernas con un abrigo corto, tal vez con plumas más largas que recubren la parte superior del cráneo o el cuello y el borde posterior de los antebrazos".

facts.statement: If present, Ornitholestes' feathers would likely have been used for insulation and possibly for incubating eggs.
facts.quote: Suponiendo que estuvieran presentes, estas plumas se habrían utilizado para aislar y posiblemente también para incubar huevos.

facts.quote: Parent group: Compsognathidae

facts.statement: Ornitholestes is classified in the family Compsognathidae.
